correctness.rationale: Definitions and all n>=9 quantifiers are explicit. Lemma 2 local closed-neighborhood inequalities imply at most one defect. The 256-state, 857-edge transfer construction is exact. A 4608-state integer shortest-path certificate checks a globally feasible potential and finds the nine reduced-cost minima; this bounds all cycle lengths, not just enumerated lengths. Nine explicit code words based at a common state splice with a zero-defect weight-7 length-9 loop, and every resulting construction selects >=4 complement vertices. Direct closed-neighborhood checks and independent exhaustive n=9,10 checks replayed from the packaged sources.

value.rationale: The published same-family problem supplied only a leading term and bounded additive error. This gives the exact invariant for every n>=9, including nontrivial period-nine offsets, improved upper constructions in six residues, and a full lower bound from a finite-state certificate. It is a natural complete classification of a key graph-identification invariant, not an arbitrary isolated table or reparameterization.
